fail_reason: Business code has fundamental device-handling bugs that prevent sdaa execution. Two mutually exclusive bugs: (1) cummins_step creates F_memory on CPU causing device mismatch; (2) compute_retardation_function uses .numpy() which fails on sdaa tensors. Cannot work around without modifying business code.

bugs_identified.description: F_memory = torch.zeros(6) creates tensor on CPU regardless of device parameter. When other tensors (M, A_inf, C, state.position) are on sdaa, this causes 'Expected all tensors to be on the same device' error.
Uses torch.linspace/torch.zeros which inherit default device. If default device is sdaa, then .numpy() calls fail. If default device is CPU, then Bug 1 occurs in cummins_step.
bugs_identified.fix: Either: (a) explicitly create tensors on CPU with device='cpu', or (b) avoid .numpy() calls and use torch operations throughout.

default_device_cpu.approach: Keep default device as CPU, pass device='sdaa' to cummins_time_integration
default_device_cpu.error: Expected all tensors to be on the same device, but found at least two devices, sdaa:0 and cpu!

default_device_sdaa.approach: Set torch.set_default_device('sdaa') so torch.zeros() creates on sdaa
default_device_sdaa.error: can't convert sdaa:0 device type tensor to numpy. Use Tensor.cpu() to copy the tensor to host memory first.

evidence_boundary: Caller-synthesised body and hydrodynamic coefficients. No LBM flow, hull coupling, free surface, or radiation-memory validation.
